title: LEGO Design — LEGO Classic House
body: Public edition. Public build reference. A sturdy little LEGO house from classic bricks. Materials: 2x4 bricks (red x24, white x24), 2x2 bricks (x16), 1x2 bricks (x20), 2x4 plates (x8), 1x1 bricks (x12), door frame 1x4x6 (x1), window frames 1x4x3 (x2), roof slopes 45-degree (x16). Steps: (1) lay a 12x16-stud baseplate footprint; (2) build the first course of 2x4 bricks around the perimeter, leaving a 4-stud door gap; (3) stack courses 2-5, offsetting joints like real brickwork; (4) set the door and window frames into courses 3-4; (5) add a plate course on top of course 5 to lock the walls; (6) build the gable ends with stepped-back bricks; (7) lay roof slopes from eave to ridge, alternating sides; (8) cap the ridge with 1x2 bricks. Tip: press each course firmly — a house that rocks has a brick not seated.
capabilities: Lay the roof slopes to the ridge

title: LEGO Design — LEGO Tower Crane
body: Public edition. Public build reference. A working-look tower crane with a rotating jib. Materials: 2x2 bricks (gray x40), 2x4 plates (x12), technic beams 1x9 (x6), technic pins (x20), 1x6 bricks (x12), string, small hook, baseplate 16x16. Steps: (1) build a 6x6-stud tower base of 2x2 bricks, 12 courses high, cross-bracing with plates every 3 courses; (2) build the turntable: a 6x6 plate ring with a center pin; (3) assemble the jib from technic beams 12 studs long, pinned at the center; (4) build the counter-jib 6 studs long with a weight box of 2x2 bricks; (5) hang the trolley string from the jib tip through a 1x1 round brick; (6) tie the hook; (7) test rotation — the jib must spin freely on the pin. Tip: keep the tower perfectly vertical; a leaning crane topples the jib.

title: LEGO Design — LEGO Race Car
body: Public edition. Public build reference. A low, fast-looking LEGO race car. Materials: 2x8 plates (black x2), 2x4 bricks (red x10), 1x2 bricks (x8), 1x1 bricks (x8), windshield slope (x1), wheels (x4), axles (x2), 1x4 tiles (x4). Steps: (1) lay the 2x8 chassis plates; (2) mount axles through 2x2 brick holders front and rear; (3) build the low nose from sloped bricks; (4) set the cockpit tub with the windshield; (5) add side pods of 1x2 bricks; (6) tile the top surfaces smooth; (7) press wheels onto axles and check they spin free. Tip: keep the center of gravity low — tall cars flip on carpet corners.

title: LEGO Design — LEGO Castle Wall Section
body: Public edition. Public build reference. A crenellated castle wall with a gate. Materials: 2x4 bricks (gray x36), 1x2 bricks (x24), 2x2 bricks (x16), 1x4 plates (x10), arch bricks 1x6 (x2), battlements 1x2 with notch (x12). Steps: (1) build two parallel 2-brick-thick walls 16 studs long; (2) fill between every 4th course with a plate tie; (3) leave a 6-stud arch gap for the gate, spanning it with arch bricks; (4) stack to 8 courses; (5) add the crenellation course — alternating 1x2 bricks and gaps; (6) cap corners with 2x2 bricks. Tip: the double wall with ties is far stronger than a single-thick wall.

title: LEGO Design — LEGO Bridge
body: Public edition. Public build reference. A beam bridge that really holds weight. Materials: 2x10 plates (x4), 2x4 bricks (x30), 1x6 bricks (x16), 2x2 bricks (x20), 1x2 technic bricks with holes (x8), technic pins (x8). Steps: (1) build two abutments of 2x4 bricks, 6 courses high, 8 studs wide; (2) lay the 2x10 deck plates across; (3) build truss sides: alternating diagonal 1x6 bricks pinned through technic bricks; (4) add the roadbed of 2x4 plates; (5) test with a book — the truss triangles carry the load. Tip: triangles are the whole secret; a flat beam sags, a truss spans.

title: LEGO Design — LEGO Treehouse
body: Public edition. Public build reference. A treehouse on a brick-built tree. Materials: brown 2x4 bricks (x30), green plates (x20), 2x2 bricks (x24), 1x4 plates (x12), ladder pieces (x4), 6x6 plate (x1). Steps: (1) build the trunk: a 4x4-stud column of brown bricks, 10 courses, with branches of 2x2 bricks; (2) spread green plates as the canopy; (3) set the 6x6 platform plate across two branches; (4) build 3-course walls on the platform; (5) add a flat plate roof; (6) hook the ladder from platform to ground. Tip: lock the platform to the trunk with plates underneath, not just studs on top.

title: LEGO Design — LEGO Space Rocket
body: Public edition. Public build reference. A classic brick rocket with stages. Materials: 2x2 round bricks (white x20), 2x2 round bricks (red x8), cone 2x2 (x1), fin slopes (x4), 1x1 round bricks (x6). Steps: (1) stack the white round bricks into the main body, 14 high; (2) add the red band courses; (3) press the cone on top; (4) attach the four fins at 90 degrees near the base; (5) the stages separate: build the booster as its own stack that the upper stage sits on. Tip: round bricks grip less than square — press straight down, never twist.

title: LEGO Design — LEGO Brick Math: Stud Grid Planning
body: Public edition. Public build reference. Planning any LEGO build starts on the stud grid: every brick's size is counted in studs, and the grid keeps builds square. Method: (1) sketch the footprint on graph paper, one square per stud; (2) mark the brick courses, offsetting joints; (3) count bricks per course from the sketch; (4) total bricks by type before building; (5) build course by course from the plan. Standard heights: a brick is 9.6 mm tall, a plate is 3.2 mm — three plates equal one brick. Tip: plan the scarce pieces first (windows, slopes), then fill walls with common bricks.
